reviewMethod: Complete line-by-line semantic review of the two GitHub issue templates, pull-request template, contributor contract, Code of Conduct, proprietary license and permanent contribution-governance policy, including local-link resolution, current roadmap authority, deterministic setup commands, exact quality gates, all four mutating API methods, private security reporting, conduct reporting and proprietary-use boundaries.

residualRisks.statement: This bounded slice reviews seven contribution-governance paths only; the remaining Batch 1 deployment, package, platform-core and script paths retain their pending status and no repository-wide completion claim is made.
Repository templates and documentation guide authorized contributors but cannot replace GitHub branch protection, required checks, reviewer enforcement or organization-level access controls.
The policy verifies committed relative-link targets and critical contribution invariants; it does not establish delivery or response-time evidence for the listed email and Telegram channels.

reviewNotes: Front matter, reproduction fields, environment context, console evidence and security-reporting boundary were reviewed line by line.
The relative SECURITY.md link resolves to the tracked root policy and the template explicitly rejects public vulnerability reports.
Problem, solution, alternatives, product-area, priority and product-principle prompts were reviewed against current repository terminology.
The priorities link now resolves directly to the official Master Roadmap v3 rather than its retained historical predecessor.

findings.attackPath: The feature template described docs/Roadmap.md as the current priorities authority even though that document is explicitly superseded, so contributors could justify work against stale phases or omit current roadmap constraints.
findings.affectedInvariant: Contribution intake must link directly to the current product authority and must not describe a retained historical document as current.
findings.evidence: docs/Roadmap.md line 3 declares itself SUPERSEDED by docs/MASTER_ROADMAP_v3.md; the template formerly linked only to the superseded path.
findings.verificationRequirement: The permanent contribution policy must require the Master Roadmap v3 target, reject the superseded target and verify the tracked local link.

reviewNotes: Change classification, affected-surface inventory, quality, security, UI, content, documentation, screenshot, test and issue-link sections were reviewed against package scripts and CI authority.
Quality guidance now uses the aggregate check command and shared-runtime test/build evidence; API guidance delegates to the exact API Security Manifest for POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE operations.

findings.attackPath: The former API/auth checklist omitted PUT from its state-changing methods and required only a direct verifyCsrfOrigin call, diverging from the API Security Manifest that governs POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE with runtime evidence and reviewed exceptions.
findings.affectedInvariant: Reviewer-facing security gates must cover the same mutating-operation set and evidence model as the executable API authority.
findings.evidence: scripts/api-security-manifest-policy.mjs defines POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE as the exact method set; the former template listed only POST, PATCH and DELETE.
findings.verificationRequirement: The permanent contribution policy must reject removal of any governed method and require both the API security check and same-origin evidence or an explicitly reviewed exception.

reviewNotes: Expected and unacceptable behavior, user-data privacy, financial-content safety, enforcement levels, reporting instructions, confidentiality statement, attribution and contact were reviewed in full.
The permanent policy rejects deletion of the reporting heading, contact address or confidentiality commitment.

Authorization, setup, branch, review, TypeScript, React, ESLint, styling, security, bilingual parity, commit, protected-surface, issue-reporting and contact guidance were reviewed against tracked files and executable package scripts.

Setup now uses the lockfile-backed registry-pinned install, starts local development without copying production configuration, and points production-like work to the governed deployment guide and untracked environment template.

findings.attackPath: The former setup used npm install despite a governed lockfile and instructed contributors to copy .env.local.example, a path that does not exist; authorized contributors could receive a non-reproducible dependency graph and stop before the first local run.
findings.affectedInvariant: The canonical contributor setup must be executable from the tracked repository and must preserve the lockfile as dependency authority.
findings.evidence: git ls-files contains .env.production.example but no .env.local.example; package-lock.json is tracked and CI installs with npm ci against the canonical npm registry.
findings.verificationRequirement: The permanent contribution policy must require the exact lockfile-backed install and production template path while rejecting npm install and .env.local.example in the setup block.

reviewNotes: Ownership, copying, commercial-use, reverse-engineering, notice, authorized-contributor, warranty, liability and contact clauses were reviewed in full.
The repository remains explicitly proprietary and confidential; this technical review does not replace legal advice or broaden any granted permission.

Input validation, rendered-Markdown comment handling, fenced-code preservation, exact invariant checks, visible local-link extraction, path normalization, repository-bound link resolution, four-method coverage and aggregated fail-closed errors were reviewed line by line.

Production-source acceptance plus negative mutations exercise hidden required text, broken links, superseded authority, incomplete API method sets, stale setup, missing gates and weakened reporting/license boundaries.

findings.attackPath: The original raw source.includes checks accepted required security, API, reporting or license text after it was moved into an HTML comment, so a GitHub template could render without the reviewer-facing gate while the permanent policy and tests remained green.
findings.affectedInvariant: Contribution governance must validate text and links visible in rendered Markdown rather than hidden source-only comments.
findings.evidence: GitHub issue and pull-request templates already use HTML comments for non-rendered prompts; wrapping a required invariant in the same syntax reproduced a false pass in the former policy.
findings.verificationRequirement: The policy must strip HTML comments outside fenced code before all required-text, forbidden-text and local-link checks, with a negative test hiding requirements in each governed document class.
